case_title: State through the Inspector of Police v. Laly @ Manikandan & Another etc.
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute (prosecution case): the accused allegedly suspected the deceased of informing on the whereabouts of a friend of the accused; relationship between accused and victim otherwise not stated
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302; IPC s.302 r/w s.34; charge sheet also cites IPC ss.341, 506(2) and s.3(1) TNPPDL Act
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW1, sole reliable eyewitness); recovery of blood-stained aruvals; postmortem and blood-stained clothing (Ex.P.16)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted A1 under s.302 IPC and A2 and A3 under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 1,000 each (default three months simple imprisonment)
high_court_outcome: Appeals allowed; convictions set aside and all accused acquitted
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 (A1); IPC s.302 r/w s.34 (A2 and A3)
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that three accused, following a dispute linked to the murder of a friend of theirs on the same day, suspected the victim of having revealed that friend's whereabouts. While the victim was travelling in a car with an eyewitness and another person, the accused, riding a two-wheeler and armed with weapons, obstructed and dashed the car, breaking its windscreen with aruvals. One accused caused an injury to the victim's right shoulder. The victim ran away to a shed, where the accused chased him and caused further injuries inside. The eyewitness stated that he saw all three accused enter the shed and then come out, leaving the victim lying injured; the victim was found dead. A complaint was given at the police station and an FIR registered on it. Investigators recovered blood-stained aruvals and conducted a postmortem. Of six eyewitnesses examined, three did not support the prosecution. The eyewitness was cross-examined at length but maintained his account.
physical_harm: Injury to the victim's right shoulder from an aruval; further injuries inside the shed; death on the spot
number_of_offences: 4 charged (IPC ss.341, 506(2), 302; TNPPDL Act s.3(1)); 2 finally upheld (IPC s.302 and s.302 r/w s.34)
motive: alleged: suspicion that the deceased had informed on the whereabouts of a friend of the accused, who had been murdered
key_evidence_accepted: Deposition of PW1, the sole eyewitness, on both the attack in the car and the attack in the shed; blood-stained aruvals and blood-stained clothing noted in the record
witness_credibility: PW1 described as star and eyewitness; fully cross-examined yet stood by his account and fully supported the prosecution; found trustworthy and reliable
trial_duration: offence: 31.07.2013; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 12.06.2018; Supreme Court: 14.10.2022
legal_representation: Accused: Rao Ranjit (Adv.); State: Dr. Joseph Aristotle S., Ms. Nupur Sharma, Shobhit Dwivedi, Sanjeev Kumar Mahara (Advs.)
investigation_status: FIR registered on complaint; investigation completed; charge sheet filed; case committed to Sessions and tried
procedural_irregularity: High Court noted complaint not marked, FIR dispatch to Magistrate at 7.00 p.m., and the constable not examined; Supreme Court held FIR timing contradictions not a ground to acquit
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted (s.302; s.302 r/w s.34). High Court: appeals allowed, accused acquitted. Supreme Court: acquittal set aside, convictions restored
prosecution_argument: PW1 is the eyewitness to both parts of the incident and fully supports the prosecution; no reason to disbelieve him; relied on Krishna Mochi
defence_argument: High Court reasons cogent; three eyewitnesses turned hostile; PW4 disbelieved; complainant Mahendran and independent witnesses not examined; contradictions on injuries; PW1 was outside the shed; weapon recovery not proved; doubt on timing and place of incident (relied on Kunju Muhammed)
legal_principle_applied: Conviction may rest on sole eyewitness testimony if trustworthy and reliable; recovery of weapon not a sine qua non; non-examination of complainant or FIR timing contradictions not grounds to discard eyewitness evidence
precedent_relied_upon: Krishna Mochi v. State of Bihar (2002) 6 SCC 81 (relied on by State); Kunju Muhammed v. State of Kerala (2004) 9 SCC 193 (cited by defence, referred to)
other_sentence_order: Accused to surrender within six weeks to undergo the sentence imposed by the trial court; failing which the Superintendent of Police/Court to take them into custody
